title: feat: adopt @miragon/modeler-api and @miragon/modeler-shell in VS Code and the web app
commits:
feat(schema-model): keep unknown fields and reject colliding ids

A document field the modeler does not know (a vendor's "x-vendor" on the
root or on an element) now passes parseDocument and is written back after
the known fields, sorted by name, nested keys too. Another tool's data
survives a save instead of being dropped.

parseDocument rejects ids that would collide on the canvas: a duplicate,
the diagram's own id tt-root, diagram-js's __implicitroot ids and
assoc_<annotation id>, the id of that annotation's connector. Such a file
used to fail halfway through the import, after the previous diagram was
already gone.

The pretty form of serializeDocument is the file on disk and now ends
with a line break, like example/sample.tt and new files; the compact form
for links and storage has none. The plugin's checker mirrors all three.

BREAKING CHANGE: parseDocument keeps unknown fields instead of stripping
them and rejects duplicate and reserved ids; serializeDocument(doc) ends
with "\n".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(renderer): vendor design system 1.13.0 and paint the canvas chrome with its roles

The token CSS, the token JSON and cd-canvas.css come unchanged from the
modeler-tool-design skill 1.13.0 and load in the guide's order: tokens,
diagram-js, cd-canvas. cd-canvas.css maps the diagram-js variables (lasso,
resize handles, popup, tooltips) onto the roles, so the renderer's own
overrides of them are gone.

Every colour of team-topologies.css is now a --cd-ui-* role, so the canvas
chrome can follow the mode together with the host's chrome. In the light
mode the roles resolve to the values used before. The palette skin applies
only to a palette no host chrome skins (data-chrome="palette"), and the
context pad takes the guide's 3px padding and 2px gap.

The drift test pins the three files to the release by hash, checks the
JSON against the CSS and accepts every --cd-* token any block declares, so
role references from the sources resolve.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(renderer): implement the modeler-api contract and the canvas rules of the modeler shell

createCollaborativeModeler and createCollaborativeViewer wrap the editor
and the NavigatedViewer in the collaborative-modeler contract of
@miragon/modeler-api 1.1.0 (notation "team-topologies"): silent, fitted
imports of the canonical document text, change events for every edit,
view state and the elements surface (teams, interactions, flows and
annotations, named by their label or text). The 1.1 conformance kit runs
in npm run test:browser with every harness hook: all 24 cases pass, no
skips, no advisories.

What the kit demanded:
- An import clears the history without a change event, suspends an open
  label edit without committing it and reopens it, with what was typed,
  on the element with the same id (L1).
- Renaming the diagram is the undoable ttModeling.setTitle command; the
  web app's title field uses it (L3).
- importDocument(doc, { fit: false }) leaves the view to a host whose
  chrome fits the diagram (L5).
- Unknown document fields ride along on the shapes and the root and are
  exported again, also after a copy (L6).
- A document whose ids would collide on the canvas is rejected before
  anything changes (L7); an import after early calls no longer trips over
  diagram-js's implicit root.

What the modeler shell asks of the canvas:
- The ttReadOnly lock vetoes move, resize, create, connect and delete and
  keeps the keyboard, context pad and label editor off the document, for
  an invalid file in an IDE host (guide 13.5).
- A palette entry triggered by the keyboard (a click with detail 0)
  creates its element in the centre of the free rectangle (freeRectCenter),
  24px further while that spot is taken, selected with its label editor
  open (guide 5.5). Entries no longer carry their own tabindex or key
  handling, and the lasso has no "Shift + drag" chip.
- The keyboard leaves zoom and fit to the chrome, ignores keys a closer
  listener handled and binds undo and redo only with undoRedoKeys (default
  true). The canvas keeps its name but no role of its own.
- The lasso icon uses the tool stroke of 2.

ICON_MENU and the other chrome-only icons, TtViewport, fitToView and
setMeta are deprecated. The stage-one web app binds the guide's zoom keys
in its zoom panel until it moves onto the shell.

BREAKING CHANGE: the canvas no longer binds +, -, Shift+0 and Shift+1;
importDocument fires no commandStack.changed, rejects colliding ids and
takes { fit }; palette entries are no tab stops and react to a click with
detail 0 instead of keydown; the canvas svg has no role="group".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(schema-model): report the path of every reason a document is invalid

A failed parseDocument now carries `issues`, each with the path of the
offending value next to the joined `error` text, so a host can point at
the exact place in the file (the VS Code extension's Problems view).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(ui): render the inspector, legend rows and shortcuts dialog into a host's chrome

The shared ui package now provides what the Team Topologies modeler puts
into the modeler shell's chrome, while the chrome places it:

- mountInspector renders the inspector's content into a host's panel
  (the shell's inspector slot), one React root for the panel's lifetime,
  and opens and closes the panel with the selection. Inspector keeps its
  own positioned panel for hosts without the shell.
- renderLegendRows fills a host's legend card with the notation's shapes,
  framework-free, with the shell's row, preview and separator classes.
- createShortcutsDialog is the Help group's "Keyboard shortcuts…" dialog
  (guide 5.4, 8): a modal <dialog> with one table per group, chips like the
  chrome tooltip's, high contrast and forced colours.
- diagramMenu builds the Export and Help groups the same in every host.

ui.css is now host-neutral content styling on the --cd-ui-* roles: no
color-scheme of its own, aliases on :root and [data-cd-theme], disabled
controls neutral instead of faded, and a focus ring instead of the blue
halo on fields (guide 8). The positioning of the web app's own inspector
and legend, its layout tokens, layers and global focus and motion rules
moved into the web app's stylesheet.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(ui): name the inspector's close key instead of a native tooltip

A native title shows only on hover, never on keyboard focus, and the
chrome's own tooltip replaces it (guide 5.6); the shell's conformance kit
rejects it. The Close button announces Escape through aria-keyshortcuts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(vscode): mount the webview on the modeler shell

The VS Code webview now runs the Team Topologies modeler inside
@miragon/modeler-shell 0.2.0 (IDE host) and the collaborative-modeler
contract: the icon-only menu, the palette skin with its keyboard model and
chrome tooltips, the zoom panel [−][NN%][+] | [Fit] with Cmd/Ctrl + + − 0
and Shift+1, the fit (never above 100 %, first import only), the problems
pill, the status box and the read-only lock of an invalid file, the
empty-file hint, and the legend and inspector slots, which the shared ui
package fills (legend rows, the React inspector). The webview's own
menu, zoom control, icons, legend state, notice and stylesheet are gone.

Extension host:
- renderWebviewHtml (lang en, appearance before the first paint) and the
  theme bridge with themes ["light"] in both editors, so a dark VS Code
  theme keeps the diagram light and high contrast passes through.
- Undo belongs to the document: the canvas binds no undo keys.
- The document's problems (JSON syntax, schema, colliding ids, dropped
  connectors) go to the Problems view and to the pill; a parse error is
  no notification any more (guide 13.5).
- Insert example writes the example as one edit (a WorkspaceEdit, or one
  CustomDocumentEditEvent in the PNG editor) and keeps the file's title.
- Fit to View, Export as PNG and Export as SVG as commands in the editor
  title's overflow, Open Source / Open Diagram to the Side, a walkthrough
  step "source", and the export notification's reveal action named like
  VS Code's.
- The host bundle targets Node 20, Geist Mono ships as font files, zod runs
  jitless under the CSP, and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md (Lucide, Feather and
  every bundled package, checked by a unit test) ships in the VSIX.

The legend's stored state moves from the webview state's top-level key to
the shell's key once.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(e2e): hold the VS Code webview to the shell kit behind a VS Code stub

The e2e suite runs two projects: `webapp` (the existing specs) and
`vscode-webview`, which serves apps/vscode/src/webview/main.ts on a Vite
test page inside the modeler shell's VS Code stub (default webview
styles, renderWebviewHtml's <html>, acquireVsCodeApi, the real theme
bridge). The webview bundle publishes nothing on window; the test page
puts its exported parts there.

- The shell conformance kit 0.2 runs for the ide host with every show
  hook (legend, problems, status, inspector, invalid) and nothing absent:
  all twelve cases pass, and any skip fails the suite.
- The webview's own behaviour: document sync and its echo, view and
  selection across outside changes, the invalid-file lock, the empty and
  blank file, the inspector and legend in the shell's slots, the legend
  state migration, exports and Command Palette commands, save and PNG
  round trips, the shortcuts dialog, the pill and keyboard creation.
- A smoke test serves the production bundle behind renderWebviewHtml's CSP
  and fails on any violation, page error or missing font.

The webview server's port is E2E_WEBVIEW_PORT, next to E2E_PORT.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs: describe the modeler shell, the contract and design system 1.13.0

CLAUDE.md, the README and CONTRIBUTING name the vendored design system
1.13.0 and its drift tests, the VS Code webview on @miragon/modeler-shell,
the @miragon/modeler-api contract with its conformance kit, the ui
package's new scope and the two e2e projects with their ports.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(ui): rename the diagram in a dialog and list the web app's own keys

What the web app's chrome needs from the shared chrome content, built for
both hosts:

- diagramMenu takes an optional editTitle and then puts "Diagram title…"
  into the Model group, before the shell's Legend checkbox. Guide §5.4
  keeps form fields out of the menu and puts no title field next to it, so
  the title the web app edited inline moves into a dialog.
- createTitleDialog(chrome, title) is that dialog (§8): one field, Cancel
  and Apply. Enter applies the trimmed title, Escape and Cancel keep it,
  an unchanged title writes nothing and a blank one cannot be applied,
  because the exports name their files after the title.
- Both dialogs share one native modal <dialog> in the shell root
  (tt-dialog: header with Close, scrolling body, footer, backdrop with
  grayscale, the high-contrast and forced-colours rules). The focus goes
  back to the control that opened a dialog, the menu trigger after a menu
  entry; a backdrop click closes only when the press started on it.
- With fileKeys the shortcuts dialog names its File rows as the menu does
  ("Open…" from the chrome's messages, "Export as JSON") and lists the
  web app's "?" under View instead of under File.
- keyboardShortcutsKey announces that key on "Keyboard shortcuts…" through
  aria-keyshortcuts only: modeler-shell 0.2 counts a chip into the entry's
  name, and its conformance kit requires a dialog entry's name to end
  with "…".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(webapp): run the web app on the modeler shell's web host

The web app mounts @miragon/modeler-shell 0.2 on its web host (pinned to
the same 0.2.0 as the other workspaces), so it looks and behaves like the
VS Code webview apart from what only the web has (guide §5.2). React
stays only inside the shell's inspector slot (the ui package's inspector);
src/main.ts is plain TypeScript around the renderer's Modeler:

- the shell's menu: File (New diagram, Open… ⌘O for .tt, .ttm.json and
  .json, Show example), Model (Diagram title…, Legend), Export (PNG, SVG,
  JSON ⌘S) and Help (Keyboard shortcuts…, also on "?", with the File
  keys), built with the ui package's diagramMenu like the webview's. The
  inline title field becomes the title dialog; Undo and Redo leave the
  menu, the canvas keeps its keys, which now also work from a chrome
  control. No Appearance group while the diagram is light-only;
- "Share" as primary action with the existing #d= link: the link goes
  into the clipboard inside the click and into the address bar, and a
  toast confirms it, warns about a very long link or points at the
  address bar;
- the zoom panel, fit and keys, the palette skin, the legend card with the
  ui package's rows (its state now persists in localStorage), the
  inspector in the shell's slot, and the legal line with www.miragon.io,
  Impressum, Datenschutz and GitHub;
- the problems pill and its list: what the importer reports (an
  annotation attached to an element that is gone), each row on its
  annotation and selecting it; a warning toast points at the pill after an
  import the visitor started;
- the start screen with the vendored, unchanged miragon-komet-blau.svg on
  a fresh visit; a page-wide drop zone for .tt, .ttm.json and .json;
- every new diagram opens like the first (viewport.newDocument), fitted
  at most to 100 %, an empty one at 100 %;
- replacing a diagram (New diagram, Show example, a file, a shared link,
  now also one pasted into the open tab) no longer asks first and no
  longer keeps a "Restore previous diagram" slot: it offers "Diagram
  replaced · Undo", also on Cmd/Ctrl+Z while the canvas has nothing else
  to undo, and an edit withdraws the offer, as in the other modelers. A
  shared link that displaces the browser's own diagram leaves that one in
  the autosave until the shared one is edited;
- toasts for every outcome, danger toasts for a file or a link that is no
  diagram, a sticky one with "Export JSON" when the storage is full;
- the tab names the diagram; index.html stays data-cd-theme="light" and
  gets the shell's head markup (theme-color, contrast line) from the Vite
  config.

The autosave key, the link format, the exports' file names and their
toasts stay. The app's own chrome (menu, title field, Share button, zoom
control, legal notice, toaster, drop zone, start card, help and confirm
dialogs, zustand stores) and app.css go, and with them zustand,
lucide-react and @vitejs/plugin-react from the app (the ui package keeps
lucide-react; Vite's Oxc compiles its JSX). A build check (npm run
check:build -w apps/webapp) fails when the built index.html lacks the
mode markup or the bundle drops the shell's Lucide licence comment, and
the root typecheck covers vite.config.ts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor(ui): drop the panels only the web app's own chrome placed

With both hosts on the modeler shell, the inspector lives in the shell's
inspector slot (mountInspector) and the legend rows in its legend card
(renderLegendRows). What only the web app's own chrome used goes:

- the standalone Inspector panel (an <aside class="tt-inspector"> the host
  had to position) and its props; InspectorSlotContent keeps every panel,
  and its tests now run through it;
- the React Legend card and legendCrowdsCanvas (the shell decides the
  legend's start state); makeRoomForLegend keeps its narrow-screen query;
- the index exports of internal helpers (useModelerSelection, Icon);
- the confirm dialog's destructive button, the legend's small close button
  and the pop-in keyframes from ui.css.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(e2e): hold the web app to the shell kit and cover its own handlers

The webapp project runs @miragon/modeler-shell's conformance kit on the
web host (webapp-shell-conformance.spec.ts): geometry at three sizes with
the primary action, the legal line, the legend, the inspector and the
raised zoom row, ARIA, keys, keyboard creation, the light-only mode under
a dark or high-contrast system, the start screen, toasts, the problems
list (rows that select their annotation), the drop zone and a clean
teardown. Team Topologies has every island of the web column, so absent
lists only "invalid": the web app edits no text and refuses a file it
cannot read before the canvas changes. onSkip throws.

webapp-chrome.spec.ts covers what the app hands the shell and its own
handlers: the start screen and the shared link, a damaged link, the menu
groups (no Appearance, no Undo), Share with and without clipboard, the
"Diagram replaced · Undo" offer (toast, Cmd/Ctrl+Z, withdrawn by an edit),
undo from a chrome control, Open… and drop, a file that is no diagram,
the title dialog, "?" for the shortcuts, Cmd/Ctrl+S, PNG and SVG exports,
import warnings in the pill and its list, the inspector in the shell's
panel, the legend's stored state, the autosave and a shared link that
keeps the own diagram in storage until it is edited. It replaces
replace-and-restore.spec.ts (the confirm dialog and the restore slot are
gone); the other specs find the canvas in the shell's slot and start from
its start screen. support/app.ts builds share links with lz-string,
pinned like the app.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(webapp): keep a replaced diagram restorable after its undo offer is gone

The "Diagram replaced · Undo" offer ends with the first edit, and that edit's
autosave wrote over the visitor's own diagram, so a shared link followed by
one edit (or New, Open, Show example) lost it for good. Before the autosave
writes over a stored diagram of another document, that diagram now moves to
the previous slot, the key 0.10 used, so its copies stay reachable. "Restore
previous diagram" leads the Model group while the browser keeps one and swaps
the two. Without room for the copy nothing is written and the storage-full
toast says autosave is paused.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(webapp): drop a problem from the pill when its element is deleted

The pill was set only on import, so deleting the annotations it named left
"2 problems" whose rows selected nothing. Every edit now recounts the import's
warnings without those of elements deleted since; an undo brings them back.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(webapp): title the start card "Team Topologies Modeler"

"Miragon Modeler for Team Topologies" wrapped to two lines on the card, where
the other modelers show their name on one. The tab and the page metadata keep
the full name.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(webapp): publish the debug globals on the dev server only

The production bundle put __ttModeler and __ttApp, its destroy() included, on
globalThis. The e2e suite and the screenshots run against the dev server, as
the VS Code webview keeps them on its test page.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(renderer): cap the palette-aware fit at 100 %

A contract host that keeps the default fit (createCollaborativeModeler without
fitOnImport: false) got the deprecated TtViewport fit, which zoomed a small
diagram up to 125 %. Guide §5.9 and the modeler shell never fit past 100 %.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(renderer): accept didi 12 as a peer

The renderer builds and tests against didi 12.0.0, and both apps ship it, but
its peer range stopped at ^11, so a consumer on didi 12 got a peer conflict.
diagram-js 15 itself still asks for didi ^11, so both majors stay allowed.
